goal: Review this repo for bugs and security issues. Produce a prioritized list with evidence.

subtasks.title: Review core app files
subtasks.instructions: Read app.py, auth.py, and server.py. Report every real bug and security issue (e.g. auth bypass, injection, unsafe deserialization, missing validation), each with the exact file and line and a short quote of the offending code.

subtasks.title: Review data and utility files
subtasks.instructions: Read search.py, storage.py, utils.py, and tests/test_utils.py. Report every real bug and security issue (e.g. SQL injection, path traversal, unsafe file handling, logic errors), each with the exact file and line and a short quote of the offending code.

subtasks.title: Review web and config files
subtasks.instructions: Read web/app.js, README.md, and requirements.txt. Report any real bugs, security issues (e.g. XSS, hardcoded secrets, outdated/vulnerable dependencies), or misconfigurations, each with the exact file and line and a short quote of the offending code.

s1.title: Review core app files

findings.title: Hardcoded admin password in source
findings.detail: Admin password is a plaintext constant in auth.py, exposing credentials to anyone with repo access.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret key for token generation
findings.detail: SECRET_KEY is a static string in source; anyone who reads the code can forge valid session tokens.

findings.title: Command injection via /export endpoint
findings.detail: User-supplied 'name' is concatenated into a shell command with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command execution.

evidence.quote: subprocess.run("tar czf exports/" + name + ".tgz books.json", shell=True)

findings.title: SSRF and disabled TLS verification on /cover endpoint
findings.detail: requests.get fetches an attacker-controlled URL with verify=False, enabling SSRF and MITM attacks.

findings.title: MD5 used for password hashing
findings.detail: MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password or token hashing; use bcrypt or SHA-256 with salt.

s1.summary: Core app files contain multiple high-severity security issues: hardcoded credentials, command injection, SSRF with disabled TLS, and weak password hashing.
s1.feedback: All five findings are on-topic, specific (file/line/quote), and supported by verified quotes. No duplication or contradiction.

s2.title: Review data and utility files
s2.reason: no final answer within the step limit

s3.title: Review web and config files

findings.title: eval() on user input (arbitrary code execution)
findings.detail: applyFilter passes the filter field value directly to eval(), allowing arbitrary JS execution in the browser.

findings.title: XSS via innerHTML with unescaped book data
findings.detail: Book title/author are concatenated into innerHTML without escaping, enabling stored XSS if data contains HTML.

findings.title: Empty catch swallows load errors
findings.detail: loadBooks catches all errors silently, hiding fetch/parse failures from the user and debugging.

findings.title: applyFilter references undefined 'books'
findings.detail: applyFilter uses a global 'books' that is never defined (loadBooks only passes it to render), so it throws ReferenceError.

s3.summary: Reviewed web/app.js, README.md, and requirements.txt. Found a critical eval() of user input, an XSS via innerHTML, and a silent empty catch; requirements.txt is minimal with no vulnerable pins.
s3.feedback: Findings are specific, each with exact file/line and verified quotes; they cover real bugs (eval on user input, XSS via innerHTML, empty catch, undefined 'books' reference) and correctly note requirements.txt has no vulnerable pins. No off-topic or exaggerated claims.
